samples.identification: SaltwaterAquarium disguise over a multi-stage .NET bitmap loader
evidence: Program.Main constructs TankForm; InitializeComponent executes the loader before finishing the aquarium UI.
InitializeComponent IL 0x728-0x7a6: get_Virtual -> CSAF.Run(bitmap,68608) -> array conversion -> AppDomain.Load -> GetTypes()[1] -> GetMethods()[0] -> VB LateCall Invoke.
CSAF.Run and its lambdas read column-order Bitmap.GetPixel(x,y), appending R, G, B. The Virtual bitmap reconstructs a valid 68608-byte managed DLL.

The DLL eW.N2.NI hex-decodes resource/key arguments, reads RcpZ from the calling assembly resources, crops 177 columns and 225 rows, serializes column-order ARGB bytes, strips a length prefix, XOR-decodes another managed assembly, loads it and invokes a selected type/method.

A reconstructed 910337-byte assembly has obfuscated delegate dispatch, encrypted resources and native process-hollowing API declarations. No specific stealer family, C2 endpoint or successful theft is asserted.

samples.identification: StormAttack native service-DLL injector and Active Setup installer; no WannaCry evidence
evidence: Entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0. Configuration byte at RVA 0x4120 is 3, selecting the Active Setup branch.

0x401900 creates an Installed Components GUID, writes HKLM Active Setup StubPath to a Windows-directory copy, reads its own image with CRT I/O, patches mode/GUID fields, writes the copy and launches it.

0x401390 constructs COMSPEC /c del using its own short module path and launches cleanup. A separate mode 4 branch at 0x401b90 attempts resource extraction and DLL injection. The fixed self-copy patch offsets do not map to the current mode field, so successful mode switching is not asserted.
0x401150 creates a hidden legitimate process, allocates/writes its DLL path remotely, resolves Kernel32.LoadLibraryA and passes it to CreateRemoteThread.
0x401260 writes LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL. The resource directory is erased in these bytes, so a usable embedded DLL and successful resource-based injection are not claimed.
The retained traits describe code/API profiles and installation mechanisms; no ransomware, encryption or DDoS execution is inferred from the family label.

samples.identification: github.com/unxed/sevenzip Go archive library with malware-bearing regression fixtures
evidence: reader_test.go TestBraRead opens testdata/pr472.7z, opens Plug 1.2/Plug 1.2.exe and io.ReadAll decompresses its contents. It never executes the member.
Source inspection found normal archive reader/writer and codec logic, with no process-execution or implant activation path.
The fixture is encrypted with the common malware-sample password infected. Its Plug 1.2 controller and Loder.dat loader contain actual Gh0st-derived malware code.
Loder.dat: 0x4017d0 connects an outbound socket; 0x401a30 sends GETSERVER; 0x401940 receives and appends the response; 0x4018b0 copies received bytes into RWX memory and starts a thread there.
Controller 0x41e710 handles GETSERVER requests; the controller embeds native modules and a configurable implant builder.

UPX-unpacked module at controller offset 0x832ebc inventories antivirus products but its force-kill loops target cmd.exe, taskmgr.exe, regedit.exe, mmc.exe and mstsc.exe. A nearby antivirus name does not make these security-product kills.
Accurate nested controller, loader and family detections remain. Their aggregation into the enclosing library does not establish a malicious library. No package or dependency allowlist was added.
PURL scans before and after used pkg:golang/github.com/unxed/sevenzip@v0.0.0-20260826171606-a536eac9d163; downloaded artifact SHA256 matched the supplied sample.

Removed a redundant remote-thread alias. Meaningful API alternatives and the remote-thread API profile are notable: references alone establish neither execution nor an unwanted boundary crossing. Removed context demotions to baseline because these remain useful capabilities in benign software.

Bound security-product force-kill detections to the actual command target, rejecting separate nearby inventories and suffix near misses.

Removed unsupported reflective-execution mapping from the UPX layout/header-check profile.
limits: Analysis was static: CIL disassembly, Ghidra and rizin; no malware was launched.
